questions.subject: androl
questions.title: Opening of the prostatic utricle
questions.question: Regarding the prostatic urethra, all of the following statements are correct EXCEPT:

options.A: It continues directly into the membranous urethra.
options.B: It is the widest part of the male urethra.
options.C: Its anterior wall carries the opening of the prostatic utricle.
options.D: Its posterior wall carries the urethral crest.

explanations.C: Correct. This is the FALSE statement, so it is the answer to the 'except' stem. The prostatic utricle and the ejaculatory ducts open on the POSTERIOR wall of the prostatic urethra, on the summit of the urethral crest (the colliculus seminalis / verumontanum), not on the anterior wall. The anterior wall is featureless.
explanations.A: Incorrect (this statement is true). The prostatic urethra runs down through the prostate and continues directly into the membranous urethra as it pierces the perineal membrane.
explanations.B: Incorrect (this statement is true). The prostatic urethra is the widest and most dilatable part of the male urethra.
explanations.D: Incorrect (this statement is true). The urethral crest is a median ridge on the posterior wall of the prostatic urethra; the prostatic utricle and ejaculatory ducts open on it at the colliculus.

questions.learning_objective: The prostatic utricle and urethral crest lie on the posterior wall of the prostatic urethra.

questions.subject: androl
questions.title: Where the bulbourethral (Cowper) gland duct opens
questions.question: The duct of the bulbourethral (Cowper's) gland opens into which part of the male urethra?

options.A: Prostatic urethra.
options.B: Periprostatic urethra.
options.C: Membranous urethra.
options.D: Spongy (penile) urethra.

explanations.D: Correct. The bulbourethral glands lie in the deep perineal pouch, but their long ducts pierce the perineal membrane and open into the proximal part of the spongy (penile) urethra within the bulb of the penis. The gland is membranous in position but its duct opens into the spongy urethra.
explanations.A: Incorrect. The prostatic urethra receives the prostatic ductules, the ejaculatory ducts and the prostatic utricle, not the bulbourethral duct.
explanations.B: Incorrect. 'Periprostatic' is not a recognised named segment of the urethra.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The gland sits in the deep perineal pouch beside the membranous urethra, but its duct runs past it to open more distally in the spongy urethra.

questions.learning_objective: The bulbourethral gland duct opens into the spongy (penile) urethra.

questions.subject: androl
questions.title: Site of the seminal colliculus
questions.question: The seminal colliculus (verumontanum) is a characteristic feature of which part of the male urethra?

options.A: Periprostatic urethra.
options.B: Membranous urethra.
options.C: Prostatic urethra.
options.D: Spongy urethra.

explanations.C: Correct. The seminal colliculus (colliculus seminalis / verumontanum) is a rounded eminence on the middle of the urethral crest, on the posterior wall of the PROSTATIC urethra. The prostatic utricle opens on its summit and the two ejaculatory ducts open on either side of it.
explanations.A: Incorrect. 'Periprostatic' is not a named urethral segment.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The membranous urethra is short and passes through the deep perineal pouch; it has no colliculus.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The spongy urethra shows the navicular fossa and the openings of the bulbourethral ducts, not the seminal colliculus.

questions.learning_objective: The seminal colliculus lies on the posterior wall of the prostatic urethra.

questions.subject: androl
questions.title: Widest and most dilatable part of the male urethra
questions.question: Regarding the male urethra, which of the following statements is TRUE?

options.A: The prostatic urethra is the widest and most dilatable part.
options.B: It is approximately 20 metres long.
options.C: The external urethral sphincter surrounds the prostatic part.
options.D: The membranous part lies in the superficial perineal pouch.

explanations.A: Correct. The prostatic urethra is about 3 cm long and is the widest and most dilatable part of the male urethra. The membranous urethra is the narrowest and least dilatable part. The external urethral orifice at the meatus is the narrowest fixed point of all.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The whole male urethra is about 18-20 CENTIMETRES long, not 20 metres.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The external urethral sphincter (sphincter urethrae) surrounds the MEMBRANOUS urethra in the deep perineal pouch, not the prostatic part.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The membranous urethra lies in the DEEP perineal pouch, piercing the perineal membrane, not the superficial pouch.

questions.learning_objective: The prostatic urethra is the widest and most dilatable part of the male urethra.

questions.subject: androl
questions.title: Length of the male urethra
questions.question: Regarding the male urethra, which of the following statements is TRUE?

options.A: It is about 20 cm long.
options.B: Its narrowest point is at the prostatic part.
options.C: Its narrowest point is at the navicular fossa.
options.D: It runs within the corpus cavernosum.

explanations.A: Correct. The male urethra is about 18-20 cm long. It extends from the internal urethral orifice at the bladder neck to the external urethral orifice at the tip of the glans. It is divided along its course into prostatic, membranous and spongy (penile) parts.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The prostatic part is the WIDEST, not the narrowest, part.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The navicular fossa is a dilatation in the glans, not a narrow point; the narrowest fixed point is the external urethral orifice (meatus).
explanations.D: Incorrect. The spongy urethra runs within the corpus SPONGIOSUM, not the corpus cavernosum.

questions.learning_objective: The male urethra is about 18-20 cm long.

questions.subject: renal
questions.title: Median umbilical ligament connects the bladder apex to the umbilicus
questions.question: Regarding the urinary bladder, which of the following statements is TRUE?

options.A: Its epithelial lining is derived from ectoderm.
options.B: Exstrophy of the bladder is due to persistence of the urachus.
options.C: It has no peritoneal covering.
options.D: Its apex is connected to the umbilicus by the median umbilical ligament.

explanations.D: Correct. The apex of the bladder is connected to the umbilicus by the median umbilical ligament. This ligament is the fibrous remnant of the urachus, the obliterated allantoic stalk. It lies in the midline and raises the median umbilical fold of peritoneum on the anterior abdominal wall.
explanations.A: Incorrect. The bladder epithelium (transitional epithelium) is derived from ENDODERM of the urogenital sinus, not ectoderm.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Exstrophy of the bladder results from failure of the infra-umbilical anterior abdominal wall (deficient cloacal membrane), whereas persistence of the urachus produces a urachal cyst or fistula.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The superior surface of the bladder is covered by peritoneum.

questions.learning_objective: The median umbilical ligament (urachus remnant) joins the bladder apex to the umbilicus.

questions.subject: renal
questions.title: Internal urethral orifice at the apex of the trigone
questions.question: Regarding the trigone of the urinary bladder, which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: It is a triangular area that appears pale in colour.
options.B: It is endodermal in origin.
options.C: The internal urethral orifice lies at its inferior angle (apex).
options.D: It lies on the inner aspect of the superior surface of the bladder.

explanations.C: Correct. The trigone is a smooth triangular area on the base (posteroinferior wall) of the bladder. Its two superolateral angles are the ureteric orifices and its inferior angle (apex), pointing downwards, is the internal urethral orifice.
explanations.A: Incorrect. Unlike the rest of the bladder the trigone mucosa is smooth and firmly adherent, but it is reddish and richly innervated, not pale.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The trigone is classically MESODERMAL in origin (absorbed mesonephric-duct ends), whereas the rest of the bladder is endodermal.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The trigone lies on the BASE (posteroinferior wall), not the superior surface.

questions.learning_objective: The internal urethral orifice is the inferior angle of the trigone.

questions.subject: renal
questions.title: Internal urethral sphincter at the bladder neck
questions.question: Which structure is located at the junction of the bladder with the urethra and is formed of smooth involuntary muscle?

options.A: Vas deferens.
options.B: Internal urethral sphincter.
options.C: Seminal vesicle.
options.D: External urethral sphincter.

explanations.B: Correct. At the bladder neck the detrusor smooth muscle is arranged as the internal urethral sphincter, an involuntary sphincter that surrounds the internal urethral orifice. In the male it also prevents retrograde ejaculation.
explanations.A: Incorrect. The vas deferens conveys sperm from the epididymis and joins the seminal vesicle duct; it is not a sphincter.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The seminal vesicle is a secretory gland behind the bladder base, not a sphincter.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The external urethral sphincter (sphincter urethrae) is voluntary skeletal muscle around the membranous urethra, not at the bladder neck.

questions.learning_objective: The internal urethral sphincter is smooth involuntary muscle at the bladder neck.

questions.subject: renal
questions.title: Sphincter urethrae and the female urethra
questions.question: Regarding the female urethra, which of the following statements is TRUE?

options.A: It is embedded in the posterior wall of the vagina.
options.B: Its lower part is surrounded by the sphincter urethrae muscle.
options.C: It is about 10 cm long.
options.D: It is derived from the mesonephric duct.

explanations.B: Correct. The female urethra is about 4 cm long and descends from the bladder neck embedded in the anterior wall of the vagina. As it passes through the deep perineal pouch its lower part is surrounded by the sphincter urethrae (external urethral sphincter). This voluntary sphincter provides the main mechanism of urinary continence in the female.
explanations.A: Incorrect. It is related to and embedded in the ANTERIOR wall of the vagina, not the posterior wall.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The female urethra is only about 4 cm long, which is why urinary tract infection is commoner in women.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The urethra develops from the urogenital sinus, not the mesonephric duct.

questions.learning_objective: The sphincter urethrae surrounds the lower female urethra in the deep perineal pouch.

questions.subject: renal
questions.title: Nerve supplying the external urethral sphincter
questions.question: A 68-year-old man developed urinary incontinence after radical prostatectomy because of paralysis of the external urethral sphincter. Which nerve was injured during the operation?

options.A: Pelvic splanchnic nerve.
options.B: Sacral splanchnic nerve.
options.C: Pudendal nerve.
options.D: Inferior gluteal nerve.

explanations.C: Correct. The external urethral sphincter (sphincter urethrae) is voluntary skeletal muscle supplied by the pudendal nerve (S2-S4), largely through its perineal branch. Injury to it during radical prostatectomy causes stress urinary incontinence.
explanations.A: Incorrect. The pelvic splanchnic nerves are parasympathetic to the detrusor and do not supply the voluntary external sphincter.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The sacral splanchnic nerves are sympathetic and supply the internal (involuntary) sphincter, not the external sphincter.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The inferior gluteal nerve supplies gluteus maximus and has no role in urethral sphincter control.

questions.learning_objective: The pudendal nerve supplies the external urethral sphincter.

questions.subject: androl
questions.title: Vas deferens crosses the ureter near the ischial spine
questions.question: Regarding the vas deferens, which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: It does not pass through the inguinal canal.
options.B: It is medial to the inferior epigastric artery at the deep inguinal ring.
options.C: It crosses the ureter in the region of the ischial spine.
options.D: It lies lateral to the seminal vesicles on the back of the bladder.

explanations.C: Correct. As the vas deferens reaches the pelvic floor near the ischial spine it crosses superior (superficial) to the ureter, before running medial to the seminal vesicle to reach the base of the prostate. This 'water under the bridge' relation mirrors the uterine artery crossing the ureter in the female. Surgeons recall it to avoid the ureter in this region.
explanations.A: Incorrect. The vas deferens is a content of the spermatic cord and does pass through the inguinal canal, entering at the deep ring.
explanations.B: Incorrect. At the deep inguinal ring the vas hooks around the LATERAL side of the inferior epigastric artery, not the medial side.
explanations.D: Incorrect. Behind the bladder the ampulla of the vas lies MEDIAL to the seminal vesicle, not lateral to it.

questions.learning_objective: The vas deferens crosses above the ureter near the ischial spine.

questions.subject: androl
questions.title: Seminal vesicle at the base of the bladder
questions.question: Which of the following structures is present at the base of the urinary bladder?

options.A: Prostate gland.
options.B: Bulbourethral gland.
options.C: Seminal vesicle.
options.D: Membranous urethra.

explanations.C: Correct. The two seminal vesicles lie on the posterior surface (base) of the bladder, lateral to the ampullae of the vasa deferentia, above the prostate. Together with the vas ampullae and the terminal ureters they are the posterior relations of the bladder base.
explanations.A: Incorrect. The prostate lies below the neck of the bladder, not on its base.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The bulbourethral glands lie in the deep perineal pouch, far below the bladder.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The membranous urethra lies in the deep perineal pouch below the prostate, not at the bladder base.

questions.learning_objective: The seminal vesicles lie on the base (posterior surface) of the bladder.

questions.subject: androl
questions.title: The tail of the epididymis lies at the lower pole of the testis
questions.question: Regarding the ductus (vas) deferens, select the WRONG statement.

options.A: It begins as a continuation of the tail of the epididymis at the upper end of the testis.
options.B: It is palpable in the spermatic cord.
options.C: It leaves the spermatic cord at the deep inguinal ring.
options.D: The ampulla of the vas lies behind the base of the bladder.

explanations.A: Correct. This is the FALSE statement, so it answers the 'wrong statement' stem. The vas deferens begins as the continuation of the tail of the epididymis at the LOWER pole of the testis, not the upper end. The head of the epididymis caps the upper pole and the tail hangs at the lower pole.
explanations.B: Incorrect (this statement is true). The firm, cord-like vas is easily palpable between finger and thumb in the spermatic cord at the neck of the scrotum.
explanations.C: Incorrect (this statement is true). The vas leaves the spermatic cord at the deep inguinal ring and hooks around the inferior epigastric artery to enter the pelvis.
explanations.D: Incorrect (this statement is true). The terminal vas dilates as the ampulla, which lies behind the base of the bladder medial to the seminal vesicle.

questions.learning_objective: The tail of the epididymis, continuous with the vas, lies at the lower pole of the testis.

questions.subject: androl
questions.title: The artery of the vas deferens arises from a vesical artery
questions.question: One of the following statements is NOT true regarding the male genital structures. Which one?

options.A: The left testicular vein drains into the left renal vein.
options.B: The artery of the vas deferens is a branch of the inferior epigastric artery.
options.C: The right testicular vein drains into the inferior vena cava.
options.D: The tunica albuginea is the fibrous coat that completely covers the testis.

explanations.B: Correct. This is the untrue statement. The artery of the vas deferens is normally a branch of the superior (or inferior) vesical artery, itself from the anterior division of the internal iliac artery, not a branch of the inferior epigastric artery.
explanations.A: Incorrect (this statement is true). The left testicular vein drains into the left renal vein, while the right drains into the inferior vena cava.
explanations.C: Incorrect (this statement is true). The right testicular vein opens directly into the inferior vena cava at an acute angle.
explanations.D: Incorrect (this statement is true). The tunica albuginea is the tough fibrous capsule that completely invests the testis.

questions.learning_objective: The artery of the vas deferens is a branch of a vesical artery (internal iliac), not the inferior epigastric.

questions.subject: androl
questions.title: The seminal vesicle secretes fluid and does not store sperm
questions.question: One of the following statements is FALSE regarding the seminal vesicle. Which one?

options.A: It lies on the posterior surface of the bladder.
options.B: Its medial surface is related to the ampulla of the vas deferens.
options.C: It acts as a reservoir for spermatozoa.
options.D: Its duct unites with the ductus deferens to form the ejaculatory duct.

explanations.C: Correct. This is the FALSE statement. Despite its name the seminal vesicle does NOT store sperm; it is a secretory gland whose alkaline, fructose-rich fluid forms most of the semen volume. Sperm are stored mainly in the tail of the epididymis and the vas deferens.
explanations.A: Incorrect (this statement is true). The seminal vesicles lie on the posterior surface (base) of the bladder above the prostate.
explanations.B: Incorrect (this statement is true). Each seminal vesicle lies lateral to, and its medial surface is related to, the ampulla of the vas deferens.
explanations.D: Incorrect (this statement is true). The duct of the seminal vesicle joins the vas deferens to form the ejaculatory duct.

questions.learning_objective: The seminal vesicle secretes seminal fluid and does not store sperm.

questions.subject: androl
questions.title: The testicular artery arises from the abdominal aorta
questions.question: Regarding the male genital structures, which one of the following statements is correct?

options.A: The testis is supplied by the testicular artery, which arises from the abdominal aorta.
options.B: The uncoiled epididymis is about one metre long.
options.C: The scrotum is drained by the para-aortic lymph nodes.
options.D: The left pampiniform plexus drains directly into the inferior vena cava.

explanations.A: Correct. The testicular artery arises directly from the abdominal aorta just below the renal arteries, reflecting the testis's high (lumbar) developmental origin before its descent. It reaches the testis through the spermatic cord.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The duct of the epididymis, if uncoiled, is about 6 metres long, not one metre.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The scrotal skin drains to the superficial inguinal lymph nodes; only the testis itself drains to the para-aortic nodes.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The left testicular (pampiniform) venous drainage is into the left renal vein; only the right drains directly into the inferior vena cava.

questions.learning_objective: The testicular artery arises from the abdominal aorta.

questions.subject: androl
questions.title: The ampulla of the vas lies medial to the seminal vesicle
questions.question: Regarding the vas deferens, choose the INCORRECT statement.

options.A: It passes through the inguinal canal.
options.B: It lies lateral to the inferior epigastric artery at the deep inguinal ring.
options.C: It lies lateral to the seminal vesicles on the back of the bladder.
options.D: Its terminal part dilates to form the ampulla of the vas deferens.

explanations.C: Correct. This is the incorrect statement. Behind the bladder the ampulla of the vas lies MEDIAL to the seminal vesicle, with the two seminal vesicles lying lateral to the two vasa; their ducts then unite to form the ejaculatory ducts.
explanations.A: Incorrect (this statement is true). The vas is a content of the spermatic cord and passes through the inguinal canal.
explanations.B: Incorrect (this statement is true). At the deep inguinal ring the vas hooks around the lateral side of the inferior epigastric artery.
explanations.D: Incorrect (this statement is true). The terminal part of the vas dilates to form its ampulla behind the bladder.

questions.learning_objective: The ampulla of the vas lies medial to the seminal vesicle behind the bladder.

questions.subject: androl
questions.title: Formation of the ejaculatory duct
questions.question: The union of the vas deferens with the duct of the seminal vesicle forms the:

options.A: Ejaculatory vesicle.
options.B: Prostatic urethra.
options.C: Seminiferous tubule.
options.D: Ejaculatory duct.

explanations.D: Correct. On each side the duct of the seminal vesicle joins the ampulla of the vas deferens to form the ejaculatory duct. The two ejaculatory ducts then pierce the prostate and open on the urethral crest beside the prostatic utricle. This is how seminal-vesicle secretion and sperm reach the prostatic urethra.
explanations.A: Incorrect. There is no structure called an 'ejaculatory vesicle'.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The prostatic urethra is the segment of the urethra within the prostate, not a duct formed by this union.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Seminiferous tubules lie within the testis and produce sperm; they are far proximal to this union.

questions.learning_objective: The ejaculatory duct is formed by the union of the vas deferens and the seminal vesicle duct.

questions.subject: androl
questions.title: Arterial supply of the prostate
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the prostate is TRUE?

options.A: The urethral crest is found on the anterior wall of the prostatic urethra.
options.B: It is supplied mainly by the inferior vesical artery.
options.C: It lies behind the base of the urinary bladder.
options.D: It has a true capsule only.

explanations.B: Correct. The prostate is supplied mainly by the inferior vesical artery (with contributions from the middle rectal and internal pudendal arteries), all branches of the internal iliac artery. Its rich venous plexus drains to the internal iliac vein and the vertebral venous plexus.
explanations.A: Incorrect. The urethral crest, with the utricle and ejaculatory-duct openings, lies on the POSTERIOR wall of the prostatic urethra.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The prostate lies BELOW the neck of the bladder, not behind its base; the seminal vesicles and vas ampullae lie behind the base.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The prostate has both a true fibrous capsule and a false capsule (condensed pelvic fascia) containing the prostatic venous plexus.

questions.learning_objective: The prostate is supplied mainly by the inferior vesical artery.

questions.subject: renal
questions.title: The ureter is a mesonephric-duct derivative
questions.question: Which of the following is a derivative of the mesonephric (Wolffian) duct?

options.A: Ureter.
options.B: Loop of Henle.
options.C: Bowman's capsule.
options.D: Prostatic urethra.

explanations.A: Correct. The ureter develops from the ureteric bud (metanephric diverticulum), which is an outgrowth of the caudal end of the mesonephric duct. It is therefore a mesonephric-duct derivative, and gives the ureter, pelvis, calyces and collecting tubules of the kidney.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The loop of Henle belongs to the nephron and develops from the metanephric blastema (mesoderm), not the mesonephric duct.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Bowman's capsule is part of the nephron, derived from the metanephric blastema.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The prostatic urethra develops from the pelvic part of the urogenital sinus (endoderm), not the mesonephric duct.

questions.learning_objective: The ureter (from the ureteric bud) is a mesonephric-duct derivative.

questions.subject: androl
questions.title: Mesonephric-duct derivative in the male
questions.question: Which of the following structures develops from the mesonephric (Wolffian) duct in the male?

options.A: Paradidymis.
options.B: Vasa efferentia.
options.C: Seminal vesicle.
options.D: Prostatic utricle.

explanations.C: Correct. The seminal vesicle is an outgrowth of the mesonephric (Wolffian) duct, which in the male also forms the epididymis, vas deferens and ejaculatory duct. Its development is driven by testosterone from the fetal testis.
explanations.A: Incorrect. The paradidymis is a vestige of the mesonephric TUBULES, not the duct.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The vasa efferentia (efferent ductules) develop from persisting mesonephric TUBULES, not the duct.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The prostatic utricle is the male homologue of the uterus/vagina and develops from the PARAMESONEPHRIC (Mullerian) ducts / urogenital sinus, not the mesonephric duct.

questions.learning_objective: The epididymis, vas deferens and seminal vesicle develop from the mesonephric duct.

questions.subject: androl
questions.title: Androgens drive mesonephric-duct development
questions.question: Regarding the genital ducts, which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: The uterus develops from the mesonephric ducts in the female.
options.B: The fetal testis produces hormones that induce growth of the mesonephric ducts.
options.C: The vas deferens develops from the mesonephric tubules.
options.D: The uterine tubes develop from the mesonephric ducts.

explanations.B: Correct. The fetal testis drives male genital-duct development by two hormones. Testosterone from the Leydig cells stimulates the mesonephric (Wolffian) ducts to form the epididymis, vas deferens and seminal vesicle. Anti-Mullerian hormone from the Sertoli cells causes the paramesonephric ducts to regress.
explanations.A: Incorrect. The uterus develops from the fused PARAMESONEPHRIC (Mullerian) ducts, not the mesonephric ducts.
explanations.C: Incorrect. The vas deferens develops from the mesonephric DUCT; the mesonephric tubules form the efferent ductules and vestiges.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The uterine tubes develop from the unfused cranial parts of the PARAMESONEPHRIC ducts.

questions.learning_objective: Testicular androgens induce mesonephric-duct development into the male genital ducts.

questions.subject: renal
questions.title: Pelvic part of the urogenital sinus forms the membranous and lower prostatic urethra
questions.question: Regarding the development of the urinary bladder and urethra, which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: The epithelium of the urinary bladder is mesodermal in origin.
options.B: The trigone is formed by absorption of the paramesonephric ducts.
options.C: The pelvic part of the urogenital sinus in the male gives rise to the membranous urethra and the lower part of the prostatic urethra.
options.D: The lowermost part of the male urethra is mesodermal in origin.

explanations.C: Correct. The urogenital sinus has three parts. The upper (vesical) part forms the bladder, and the phallic part forms the spongy urethra. The pelvic part forms the whole female urethra and, in the male, the membranous urethra plus the lower part of the prostatic urethra.
explanations.A: Incorrect. The bladder epithelium is derived from ENDODERM of the urogenital sinus, not mesoderm.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The trigone is formed by absorption of the caudal ends of the MESONEPHRIC (not paramesonephric) ducts.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The lowermost (glandular) part of the male urethra is ECTODERMAL, formed by an ingrowth of surface ectoderm at the glans.

questions.learning_objective: The pelvic part of the urogenital sinus forms the membranous and lower prostatic urethra in the male.

questions.subject: renal
questions.title: Incomplete division of the ureteric bud causes a bifid ureter
questions.question: Incomplete division of the metanephric diverticulum (ureteric bud) results in:

options.A: Bifid ureter and a supernumerary kidney.
options.B: A bifid kidney.
options.C: Complete duplication of the ureter.
options.D: A bifid ureter.

explanations.D: Correct. Premature but INCOMPLETE division of the ureteric bud produces a Y-shaped bifid ureter, in which two ureters join before entering the bladder by a single orifice. It is usually asymptomatic.
explanations.A: Incorrect. A supernumerary (extra) kidney with a completely separate ureter results from an accessory ureteric bud, not from incomplete division of one bud.
explanations.B: Incorrect. 'Bifid kidney' is not the recognised term for this ureteric-bud anomaly.
explanations.C: Incorrect. COMPLETE early division of the ureteric bud gives a completely duplicated ureter with two separate orifices, not a bifid ureter.

questions.learning_objective: Incomplete division of the ureteric bud produces a bifid ureter.

questions.subject: gyn
questions.title: The genital tubercle forms the clitoris in the female
questions.question: Regarding the development of the external genitalia, which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: The genital tubercle elongates slightly in the female to form the clitoris.
options.B: The genital (labioscrotal) swellings form the labia minora in the female.
options.C: Hypospadias is an abnormal urethral meatus on the dorsum of the penis.
options.D: The most distal part of the penile urethra is endodermal in origin.

explanations.A: Correct. The genital tubercle is the midline swelling at the cranial end of the cloacal membrane. In the male it enlarges under androgens to form the glans penis. In the female, with little androgen, it elongates only slightly to form the clitoris.
explanations.B: Incorrect. The labioscrotal (genital) swellings form the labia MAJORA in the female (and the scrotum in the male); the labia minora form from the urogenital folds.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Hypospadias is an abnormal urethral opening on the VENTRAL surface of the penis; a dorsal opening is epispadias.
explanations.D: Incorrect. The most distal (glandular) part of the penile urethra is ECTODERMAL, from an ingrowth of surface ectoderm.

questions.learning_objective: The genital tubercle forms the clitoris in the female and the glans penis in the male.

questions.subject: androl
questions.title: The glandular part of the male urethra is ectodermal
questions.question: Regarding the development of the urinary bladder and urethra, all of the following statements are correct EXCEPT:

options.A: The trigone of the bladder is formed by absorption of the mesonephric ducts.
options.B: The urachus extends from the apex of the developing bladder to the umbilicus.
options.C: The pelvic part of the definitive urogenital sinus in the male gives rise to the membranous urethra and the lower part of the prostatic urethra.
options.D: The lowermost part of the male urethra is endodermal in origin.

explanations.D: Correct. This is the FALSE statement, so it answers the 'except' stem. The lowermost (glandular / navicular) part of the male urethra is ECTODERMAL, formed by an ingrowth of surface ectoderm at the glans that canalises to join the endodermal spongy urethra. The rest of the urethra is endodermal.
explanations.A: Incorrect (this statement is true). The trigone forms by absorption of the caudal ends of the mesonephric ducts.
explanations.B: Incorrect (this statement is true). The urachus runs from the bladder apex to the umbilicus and persists as the median umbilical ligament.
explanations.C: Incorrect (this statement is true). The pelvic part of the urogenital sinus forms the membranous and lower prostatic urethra in the male.

questions.learning_objective: The glandular (distal) part of the male urethra is ectodermal in origin.

questions.subject: gyn
questions.title: Uterus didelphys
questions.question: A double uterus with a double vagina, resulting from complete failure of fusion of the paramesonephric ducts, is called:

options.A: Uterus didelphys.
options.B: Uterus bicornis bicollis.
options.C: Uterus bicornis unicollis.
options.D: Septate uterus.

explanations.A: Correct. The uterus and upper vagina form by fusion of the lower parts of the two paramesonephric ducts. Complete failure of this fusion produces uterus didelphys. There are then two separate uterine bodies, two cervices and (usually) a double vagina.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Uterus bicornis bicollis has two horns and two cervices but the ducts have partly fused, so it is less complete than didelphys.
explanations.C: Incorrect. Uterus bicornis unicollis has two horns but a single cervix and vagina.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A septate uterus has a normal external outline with a persistent internal septum from failure of resorption, not failure of fusion.

questions.learning_objective: Complete failure of paramesonephric fusion produces uterus didelphys (double uterus and vagina).

questions.subject: gyn
questions.title: Uterus bicornis unicollis
questions.question: A double uterus with a single cervix and a single vagina is called:

options.A: Uterus didelphys.
options.B: Uterus bicornis bicollis.
options.C: Uterus bicornis unicollis.
options.D: Septate uterus.

explanations.C: Correct. The lower parts of the paramesonephric ducts fuse normally to form a single cervix and vagina. Failure of fusion limited to the upper parts then produces uterus bicornis unicollis. This gives two uterine horns opening into a single cervix and vagina.
explanations.A: Incorrect. Uterus didelphys has two cervices and a double vagina, reflecting a more complete fusion failure.
explanations.B: Incorrect. Uterus bicornis bicollis has two horns AND two cervices.
explanations.D: Incorrect. A septate uterus has a single normal external outline with an internal septum, from failed resorption rather than failed fusion.

questions.learning_objective: A double uterus with a single cervix and vagina is uterus bicornis unicollis.
